title: Pulsecard — 14-day output & quick retro
content:
Pulsecard (14d) — quick running notes, not a polished doc

Context: two-week pulsecard to help me keep small bets alive and reduce churn on experiments. Using this as my 14-day checkpoint before I update OKRs. Mostly for tracking hypotheses, tiny metrics, blockers, and next micro-commitments.

What I tracked (metrics snapshot)
- Focus hours (deep work, scheduled 90m slots): target 18, actual 15.5 — notes: must protect Wednesday morning and Friday afternoon.
- PRs merged: target 4, actual 3 (1 stacked PR blocked by infra flaky tests).
- Customer calls / feedback docs contributed: 2 (one notes doc added to cs-playbook).
- Small experiments launched: 3 (see experiments list).
- Confidence on owning "developer onboarding flow" KR: 40% -> 55% (move from discovery to first implementation).

Micro-KPIs I care about (and why)
- Time-to-first-success: median minutes for a new dev to run local inference example (baseline 45m). Why: onboarding friction -> adoption.
- Cold-start latency SLO presence: did we get a reproducible test harness set? (binary)
- Experiment velocity: days between idea -> canary (goal < 7d)

Hypotheses (short)
- H1: If I reduce setup steps from 12->8 (remove optional env flags + add checklist), time-to-first-success will drop by ~25% for new engineers.
- H2: A focused README with 3 quick-run commands will convert >50% of trial attempts into a local run vs zero-run.

Experiments (launched / in-flight)
1) README Minimal: trimmed local dev README to 3 commands + one troubleshooting bullet. (launched 2026-03-01)
   - Metric: local-run completion via self-report + small survey (n=8 so far). Early result: 5/8 succeeded within 60m.
   - Next: add short GIF and move into platform quickstarts.
2) Setup checklist script: bootstrap.sh auto-installs minimal deps in container (WIP)
   - Blocker: infra runner image mismatch (ticket INF-842). Need infra review from Ben.
3) Onboarding office hours: 2 slots this sprint, measured attendance and run-rate.

Wins (small, tangible)
- Got the README trimmed without losing advanced notes — feedback from Asha that it reduced confusion.
- One new engineer got local example running in a single session (celebrate).

Blockers / friction
- Flaky CI prevents merging PR #1034 (failing integration e2e on macos runner). Dependent on release-engineering triage.
- Time fragmentation: meetings encroaching on planned focus slots (Monday afternoons).

Action items (next 14d) — prioritized
- A1: Fix bootstrap image mismatch with infra (owner: Ben) — FYI p1. (linked INF-842)
- A2: Add GIF and one-line quickstart to platform quickstarts (owner: me) — due 03/20
- A3: Schedule 2 more office hours and collect short surveys after each (owner: me)
- A4: Add one e2e smoke harness for local example to catch macos runner issue earlier (owner: me + release-eng)

Smaller commitments (notes to self)
- Try 2 Pomodoro-style 25/5 during focus slots next week to see if squeezing helps concentration.
- Turn one long meeting into async update where possible — test with weekly sync owners.

Risk & mitigation
- Risk: shipping a "too minimal" README loses advanced users (frustration). Mitigation: keep an "advanced" link and surface common advanced flags in troubleshooting.

Questions for leads / ask list
- Ben: can release-eng triage INF-842 this sprint? Timing will determine whether stacked PRs move.
- Asha: want to review the quickstart GIF copy before I land it?

Random ideas / backlog (parking lot)
- Short video walk-through (3 min) for the quickstart — maybe use Loom.
- Small test harness that records a short trace of the local run to help debugging.

Final quick retro (one-line)
- Energy: ok but spread thin; wins from simplification visible; focus on removing the infra friction and shipping GIF + checklist to get momentum back.

Appendix: quick links
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1034
- Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-842
- Confluence draft: /display/ENG/Personal+OKR+notes

Notes-to-self: keep this pulsecard short, update every 14 days, use it to convert ideas into next-step checklists.
